evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: No other story in the backlog expresses creating a new game with name/optional description.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: No other story duplicates the specific act of inviting via a URL.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: While other stories cover adding items, none require starting a round via a single multi-line input.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Similar theme appears for estimators, but actor/context differ (moderator), so not a duplicate.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: No other story exactly duplicates the moderator selecting an item for estimate/re-estimate.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to the list is distinct from starting a round or editing/deleting items.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item is not duplicated by any other story (add/delete/select are distinct).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deletion is a distinct action (no duplicate story expressing same deletion requirement).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This describes forcing an immediate reveal even if not all estimators have acted; no other story duplicates this behavior.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting the average is a distinct business rule not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: estimate field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatic acceptance when all cards match is a specific behaviour not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Manual entry of agreed estimate is distinct from automatic behaviours or acceptance rules elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Substantially contained by PP-005 which already specifies selecting an item to be estimated or re-estimated (same actor, context and goal).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories as a spreadsheet operation is not duplicated by other backlog items (copy/paste is a separate mechanism).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste is a distinct method from an import feature; not a duplicate requirement.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing past games is different from viewing/exporting transcripts; no duplicate requirement.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript is distinct from browsing or exporting; no other story duplicates viewing specifically.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export to HTML is a specific format requirement and not a duplicate of CSV export or viewing.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export to CSV is a distinct format requirement from HTML export.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game is a unique requirement; no other story duplicates game deletion.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation with specified fields is not duplicated by other backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login is a distinct requirement, not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Account modification is unique compared to creation, deletion, or login.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion differs from deleting a game and is not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display requirement is distinct and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder by email is a unique authentication recovery requirement.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {sequence A} or {sequence B}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing estimation scale sequences is a specific configuration not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A capacity limit on invites is a unique constraint not duplicated by other invite-related stories.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL
evaluations.rationale: Estimator-side joining via the URL page is distinct from the moderator sending the URL.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Estimator needing to see the current item is distinct and not duplicated by moderator actions.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Estimator view of the session's items differs by actor/context from the moderator's similar story (PP-004).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Immediate presence/indicator of who has acted is distinct from viewing actual estimates.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This requirement (reveal after all have given) is different from immediate reveal or moderator-forced reveal.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Functionally equivalent to PP-041 which already allows changing an estimate while the draw is not completed (same actor/context/goal).

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates for a participant is a different requirement from other estimate-viewing stories.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Seeing which person gave which estimate during the current round is distinct from immediate presence or prior estimates.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer start capability is separate from timer reset behaviour; no duplicate exists.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-reset behavior is a specific requirement distinct from starting a timer.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: History/scrollback is unique and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering persistence is a unique UI requirement not expressed elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This phrasing is accepted as the canonical change-before-reveal requirement; PP-034 is a duplicate of it.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Thumbnail personalization is a unique UI requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is distinct from browser-specific compatibility requirements.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary/definitions list is a distinct documentation requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing as an implementation requirement is not duplicated by other performance or UX stories.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Supporting specific legacy browsers is a distinct requirement from general standards compliance or accessibility.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is distinct from browser/version support or XHTML/CSS compliance.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: General performance/UX responsiveness is distinct from technical tasks like indexing.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a unique internationalization requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design/structure requirement is distinct and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Friendly error pages are a unique UX requirement not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymized storage for research is a specific privacy requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Analytics/metrics viewing is a distinct requirement and not duplicated in the backlog.
